_comment: Art that proves the game HUD is on screen, i.e. that we are actually in play.
TWO references, on OPPOSITE CORNERS, and EITHER ONE is enough. A single reference made
the check fragile to anything covering it: hovering an item draws a tooltip over the
right-hand orb and the score fell to 0.48, so the pipeline decided it was not in a game
and paused everything - while the left orb sat there in plain view.
Occlusion is normal during play (tooltips, panels, spell effects) and it is local, so
the fix is a second piece of evidence somewhere else rather than a looser threshold.
Measured on the frame where the single reference failed:
right orb frame (gargoyle)  0.48   <- covered by the tooltip
and on two lobby frames, where NEITHER may match: gargoyle 0.27/0.33, angel 0.37/0.37.
region and search_region are fractions of the ANCHOR WINDOW (see window_region.py), so
they survive the game being windowed, moved or resized.
